correctness.rationale: For a deletion graph without isolates, size-three total dominating sets have one full vertex and a pair covering the opposite part. If a full larger-side vertex remains and gamma_t>=4, all smaller-side missing-neighbor sets are pairwise intersecting and have size at least two; this yields the sharp \(2a\) lower bound, with the \(a=2\) obstruction. A surjective single-deletion-per-column construction uses b edges, and a three-column triangle construction uses 2a edges, both preserving positive degrees and excluding every size-two/three total dominating set. Equality forces surjections or pairwise-intersecting two-sets on three columns, counted exactly by \(a!S(b,a)\) and \(\binom b3\,3!S(a,3)\). Boundary \(b=2a\) is the disjoint union of the two families. The extracted Python checker independently enumerated all deletion masks and all vertex subsets of size 2/3 on 14 small cases and verified predicted counts; the proof itself treats all a,b.

value.rationale: The new exact high-imbalance equality completes the natural complete-bipartite two-total bondage problem studied in a 2025/2026 paper, with an explicitly sharp transition at \(b=2a\). The complete labelled extremizer classification reveals genuinely different failure mechanisms: full-degree elimination via a surjection, versus a three-column pair-cover design. Their exact Stirling counts and coexistence at the threshold are structural information not determined by prior scalar bounds. The object and invariant are motivated by robustness of total domination under edge failure, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
